topics.title: Introduction, Purpose, and Benefits of Cash Flow Statement
explain: A Cash Flow Statement summarizes historical changes in cash and cash equivalents over a specific accounting period.
It classifies cash flows into three activities: Operating, Investing, and Financing.
It provides vital information to evaluate an enterprise's liquidity, solvency, and quality of earnings.
The primary purpose is to explain cash movements between two balance sheet dates.
Major sources of cash include issuing shares, selling fixed assets, and operating profits.
Major applications of cash include redeeming shares, purchasing fixed assets, paying taxes, and paying dividends.

flow.title: Tracking Cash Flow Across a Financial Period
steps: Record cash balance at period start
Add cash inflows from core operations
Add proceeds from asset sales and loans
Deduct cash paid for assets and expenses
Reconcile with closing cash balance

topics.example: Comparing your bank balance on the 1st and 31st of the month to see how much income came in and where expenses went.
remember: AS 3 governs the preparation and presentation of Cash Flow Statements.
The statement explains cash movements between two points of time.
mistakes: Confusing net accounting profit with actual net cash generated during the period.

quiz.q: What is the primary purpose of a Cash Flow Statement under AS 3?
o: To compute total income tax liability
To explain cash movements between two points of time
To record daily credit sales transactions
quiz.why: A cash flow statement explains how cash moved between the opening and closing balance sheet dates.

quiz.q: Which of the following is classified as a source of cash?
o: Purchase of property, plant, and equipment
Issue of equity shares and debentures
quiz.why: Issuing shares or debentures brings cash inflow into the enterprise.

topics.title: Elements of Cash and Cash Equivalents
explain: 'Cash' comprises cash in hand and demand deposits held with banks.
'Cash equivalents' are short-term, highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash.
They must carry an insignificant risk of changes in value.
Securities usually qualify as cash equivalents if they have a short maturity of 3 months or less from the acquisition date.
Their primary objective is to deploy idle cash temporarily to meet short-term cash commitments.
Transactions moving funds between cash, bank demand deposits, and cash equivalents are not cash flow activities.

flow.title: Test to Qualify an Item as a Cash Equivalent
steps: Verify investment is short-term and liquid
Check maturity is 3 months or less
Confirm insignificant risk of value change
Classify item as a Cash Equivalent

topics.example: Holding a 60-day treasury bill or a short-term bank deposit to meet upcoming wage payments.
remember: Maturity period must be 3 months or less from the date of acquisition.
Depositing cash into a bank current account is not a cash flow activity.
mistakes: Including equity shares or long-term investments with price volatility as cash equivalents.

quiz.q: What is the maximum maturity period from the acquisition date for an investment to qualify as a cash equivalent under AS 3?
quiz.why: AS 3 requires cash equivalents to have a short maturity of 3 months or less from the date of acquisition.

quiz.q: Withdrawing cash from a bank current account for office use is classified as:
quiz.why: It is a movement between components of cash and cash equivalents, not a cash flow activity.

topics.title: Classification of Cash Flow Activities
explain: AS 3 requires cash flows to be classified into Operating, Investing, and Financing activities.
Cash inflows result in a cash increase, while cash outflows result in a cash decrease.
Operating activities are the principal revenue-generating activities of the business entity.
Investing activities relate to the acquisition and disposal of long-term assets and other non-cash equivalent investments.
Financing activities result in changes in the size and composition of the owner's capital and borrowings.

flow.title: Classifying Cash Flow Transactions
steps: Analyze transaction details
Check if core revenue-generating activity
If not, check if long-term asset related
If not, check if capital or borrowing related
Assign to Operating, Investing, or Financing

topics.example: Selling inventory is operating, purchasing machinery is investing, and taking a bank loan is financing.
remember: Financing = Owner's capital and borrowing changes.
mistakes: Classifying interest paid by a manufacturing entity as an operating activity instead of a financing activity.

quiz.q: Which activity category includes principal revenue-generating activities of an enterprise?
quiz.why: Operating activities are the primary revenue-producing operations of an enterprise.

quiz.q: Transactions that alter the equity capital and borrowings of a company are classified as:
quiz.why: Financing activities alter the size and structure of owner's capital and borrowings.

topics.title: Operating Activities and Calculation Methods
explain: Operating cash flow shows if core operations generate enough cash to maintain capability, pay dividends, and make new investments.
Direct Method lists major classes of gross cash receipts (e.g., from customers) and gross cash payments (e.g., to suppliers).
Indirect Method adjusts Net Profit/Loss before tax for non-cash items, non-operating items, and working capital changes.
Non-cash items like depreciation and goodwill amortisation are added back to net profit.
Working capital changes adjust net profit: add decreases in current assets and increases in current liabilities.
Income tax paid is deducted separately under operating activities unless specifically linked to investing/financing.

flow.title: Indirect Method Steps for Operating Cash Flow
steps: Start with Net Profit before Tax
Add non-cash expenses like depreciation
Deduct non-operating income like gain on sale
Adjust for working capital asset/liability changes
Deduct actual income tax paid

topics.example: Adding back ₹37,000 depreciation to net profit and deducting ₹34,000 inventory increase to find net cash from operations.
remember: Direct method uses gross cash receipts and payments.
Indirect method adjusts net profit for non-cash and working capital items.
mistakes: Subtracting an increase in trade payables instead of adding it in the indirect method.

quiz.q: Under the Indirect Method of AS 3, depreciation expense is:
quiz.why: Depreciation is a non-cash expense previously deducted in profit calculation, so it must be added back.

quiz.q: In operating cash flow calculations, an increase in inventory during the year is:
quiz.why: An increase in inventory represents cash used to acquire stock, so it is a cash outflow.

topics.title: Investing Activities
explain: Investing activities show expenditures made for resources intended to generate future income and cash flows.
Cash outflows include purchasing fixed assets (including capitalized R&D), intangibles, and buying shares/debentures of other entities.
Cash inflows include selling property, plant, equipment, intangibles, and debt/equity instruments of other entities.
For non-financial companies, interest received and dividend received are classified as investing cash inflows.
Loans and advances made to third parties or subsidiaries (and their repayments) are investing activities for non-financial entities.

flow.title: Processing Cash Flows from Investing Activities
steps: Identify long-term asset & investment transactions
Record cash paid for purchases as outflow
Record cash received from sales as inflow
Include interest and dividend receipts
Compute Net Cash from Investing Activities

topics.example: Receiving ₹1,02,000 from selling investments costing ₹90,000 is an investing cash inflow.
remember: Purchases of fixed assets and investments are outflows; sales are inflows.
For non-financial firms, interest and dividend received are investing cash inflows.
mistakes: Treating purchase of shares held for trading/dealing purposes as investing instead of operating activities.

quiz.q: Cash received from the sale of an old plant and machinery is classified as:
quiz.why: Disposal of long-term property, plant, and equipment is an investing activity.

quiz.q: For a non-financial company, dividend received on investments in another company is an:
quiz.why: Income generated from holding long-term investments is classified under investing activities.

topics.title: Financing Activities
explain: Financing activities cover transactions that change the size and composition of owner's capital and borrowings.
Cash inflows include proceeds from issuing equity shares, preference shares, debentures, loans, and bonds.
Cash outflows include repayment of loans, redemption of preference shares/debentures, dividend paid, and interest paid.
For non-financial entities, dividend paid and interest paid are financing cash outflows.
Payments by a lessee for reducing outstanding finance lease liabilities are financing cash outflows.
Significant non-cash financing transactions (e.g., issuing shares to acquire assets or convert debentures) are excluded from the statement but disclosed.

flow.title: Calculating Net Cash from Financing Activities
steps: Identify capital and loan transactions
Add cash proceeds from issuing shares or loans
Deduct cash paid for loan repayments
Deduct dividends and interest paid
Calculate Net Cash from Financing Activities

topics.example: Paying ₹50,000 to repay bank bonds and ₹8,000 cash dividend to shareholders are financing outflows.
remember: Dividend paid is ALWAYS a financing cash outflow.
Non-cash transactions (like converting debentures to equity) are excluded from cash flow calculations.
mistakes: Including non-cash transactions like equity shares issued for asset acquisition in the cash flow statement.

quiz.q: Dividend paid by a non-financial enterprise is classified in the cash flow statement as a:
quiz.why: Paying dividend is a cash outflow related to servicing owner's capital.

quiz.q: How is the conversion of debentures into equity shares reported in the Cash Flow Statement under AS 3?
o: Excluded from cash flow statement as a non-cash item
quiz.why: Transactions that do not involve cash flow are excluded from the Cash Flow Statement and disclosed separately.
